issues.translation_quote: Domino!
issues.justification: In the domino game 'рыба' is a blocked game; 'Domino!' is the wrong call and loses the term.

issues.translation_quote: Doubles out. That's how we play.
issues.justification: Domino context: 'отдуплились' means playing off the doubles; 'Doubles out' is unclear, and the 'Got one' rendering of 'Есть такая' is also unclear.

issues.source_quote: Роза Муда - шент мир дер херц унд дер я. Роза Муда - франк ду них мерт ди мама. Роза Муда - глауб мир аргер детрай.
issues.translation_quote: Rosa Muda — schenk mir dein Herz und sag ja. Rosa Muda — frag doch nicht mehr die Mama. Rosa Muda — glaub mir, ärger dich nicht.
issues.justification: The source is deliberately garbled pseudo-German nonsense (macaronic joke); the translation invents clean German, losing the gibberish effect.

issues.source_quote: Был я конкурсе я джазов, обалдел от джазов сразу.
issues.translation_quote: I went to a jazz contest, jazz knocked me silly on the spot.
issues.justification: Soev's deliberately clumsy, ungrammatical verse (and the pun 'джазов' used as a plural) is smoothed out; the parody of bad poetry is lost. Also 'два джаза ... дули' mistranslated as jazz bands blew.

issues.translation_quote: Youth, you seek for love, burning with desire
issues.justification: Minor in meaning, but the lecture on Phalaecian hendecasyllable contains the poem used as a demonstration of meter; the English version ignores meter entirely and the metric terms ('четырех хореев и одного тактеля' → 'dactyl') are altered, which is inaccurate.

issues.translation_quote: Émile Zola died of fumes.
issues.justification: 'Угорел' means suffered carbon monoxide poisoning; the joke referencing Zola's real death is blunted, and the following 'turn off the gas burners' is only half supported.

issues.translation_quote: They've found the skull of Prophetic Oleg's horse.
issues.justification: 'Вещий Олег' is a standard epithet; 'Prophetic Oleg' is unidiomatic, and the cultural reference (Pushkin ballad) is unexplained, so the joke is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Был я конкурсе я джазов... Тунеядца хоронили
issues.translation_quote: They buried a freeloader, his girlfriends wept... And two jazz bands at his grave blew
issues.justification: 'Подруги' and the pun with 'дули' (blew / gave the fig) are flattened; the parody couplet loses its absurd humor.

issues.translation_quote: Want to settle it by the Hamburg score?
issues.justification: 'По гамбургскому счету' is an idiom meaning 'honestly, by true standards'; literal rendering is meaningless in English.

issues.translation_quote: There lay the cold war, brothers.
issues.justification: Wordplay (cold war lying under couch; Soev's stale content) is retained, but 'Bony, toothless and browless' parodies are fine; however 'имел я селёдку' kept literally 'had a herring' loses nonsense nuance. Questionable fidelity.

issues.translation_quote: Auf Wiedergucken.
issues.justification: Transliteration of the pseudo-German joke is kept, but without any cue the English audience cannot see the play on 'gucken'.

issues.translation_quote: Sporty cheers!
issues.justification: The Soviet-era greeting 'Физкульт-привет' has an epoch flavor that 'Sporty cheers' does not convey.

issues.source_quote: Благодарю вас... О, благодарю... Мне было так хорошо... Я рада... Вы так это делали...
issues.translation_quote: Thank you... Oh, thank you... That felt so good... I'm glad... The way you did it...
issues.justification: The double-entendre scene, where the nurse's injections sound erotic, is partly kept but 'You give marvelous injections' reads overly clinical in the second line.

issues.source_quote: Это жизнь. Один завоевывает кубки, другой гравирует на них его имя.
issues.translation_quote: Way to go!
issues.justification: 'Вот дает!' rendered as 'Way to go!' misreads the intended tone (amazement at the spat story) and sounds anachronistically American.

issues.translation_quote: Sing, swallow, sing.
issues.justification: Satirical couplet parodies Soviet propaganda verse; the English loses rhyme and meter, weakening the parody.

issues.source_quote: Вы, как судьи, нарисуйте наши судьбы
issues.translation_quote: Like judges, paint our destinies
issues.justification: Song lyric loses rhyme and rhythm entirely; the poetic register is flattened.

issues.translation_quote: Trading in flesh?
issues.justification: Velyurov's quip about 'creating new torsos' is rendered awkwardly; 'Trading in flesh' sounds heavier than the playful insinuation.

issues.source_quote: Как же, пожилым надо уступать. Спасибо, девочка.
issues.translation_quote: Of course it is, you give up seats to the elderly. Thank you, little girl.
issues.justification: The comic sequence of Lev being offered a seat is made confusing by the assigned lines.

issues.translation_quote: Natürlich
issues.justification: Mixing German interjections inconsistently ('Fünf Minuten' vs 'Ein Moment') without cue slightly confuses the running gag of Savva's German.

issues.source_quote: - Я не порядочен? Тогда говори! - Безусловно.
issues.translation_quote: - I'm not decent? Then say it! - Absolutely not.
issues.justification: Margarita is confirming that he is indecent ("Certainly, you are not decent"). "Absolutely not" reverses the sense and implies she denies it.

issues.source_quote: Вонзил кинжал убийца нечестивый в грудь деларю. Тот, шляпу сняв, сказал ему учтиво: благодарю!
issues.translation_quote: The impious assassin plunged his dagger into the breast of De Larue. Who, doffing his hat, said politely: thank you!
issues.justification: The parody depends on the rhyme "Деларю / благодарю" and the comic politeness. The translation drops the rhyme and the name sounds odd, so the joke and the verse form are lost.

issues.translation_quote: the Pokrov Gate
issues.justification: The standard rendering is "Pokrovsky Gates" (the film's English title). "Pokrov Gate" is non-standard and singular.

issues.translation_quote: Lev Evgenyevich / Lev Yevgenyevich
issues.justification: The patronymic is transliterated inconsistently within the same text.

issues.source_quote: Очень жаль, что вы не грассируете.
issues.translation_quote: you don't roll your R's like the French
issues.justification: Grasseyer means a uvular or guttural R, not rolling the R. "Roll your R's" describes a trill, which is a different sound.

issues.translation_quote: He won't abandon his steel friend.
issues.justification: The phrase is a jocular epithet (the iron/steel friend, i.e. his car or machine). The literal "steel friend" is opaque in English.

issues.translation_quote: I look like some kind of hipster.
issues.justification: "Стиляга" is a specific 1950s Soviet subculture. "Hipster" carries modern connotations and weakens the period feel.

issues.source_quote: Боритесь за права мужчины и человека!
issues.translation_quote: Fight for the rights of man and male!
issues.justification: The line plays on "rights of man and citizen". "Man and male" is clumsy and loses the mock-solemn echo.

issues.source_quote: Где ежеминутно будут исчезать неведомо куда квитанции, счета, деньги, чулки и галстуки?
issues.translation_quote: Where every minute, vanishing God knows where, will be receipts, bills, money, stockings and ties?
issues.justification: The inverted syntax is awkward and unnatural in English for Margarita's rapid, indignant speech.

issues.source_quote: Хотя, согласись, что твое состояние от холодного далеко.
issues.translation_quote: Though, you must admit, your state is far from cool-headed.
issues.justification: The sense is unclear and the joke is not preserved. The line plays on his normal temperature against his agitated state, and "cool-headed" shifts the meaning.

issues.translation_quote: Loneliness and novels.
issues.justification: The bookish, ironic "беллетристика" is flattened to "novels", losing some of the speaker's affected register.

issues.translation_quote: You'll give this perfume to Mum.
issues.justification: British "Mum" and "flat" are mixed with American "pajamas" and "color", so the variant of English is inconsistent.
